chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn ibn Saeed, from Fazalat ibn Ayoub, from Rafa'ah who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the walking of Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) — was it from Makkah or from Al-Madina? He said: 'From Makkah'. And I asked him, 'When I visit the House, should I ride or walk?' So he said: 'Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) used to visit riding'. And I asked him about riding, whether it is superior or the walking? So he said: 'The riding'. I said, 'The riding is superior than walking?' He said: 'Yes, because Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) rode'.
ai.seo_question: Is it better to walk or ride during Hajj according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* highlights the juristic preference (*fada'il*) for riding during Hajj, grounded in the precedent of Imam Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) and the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family). The reasoning provided—that riding is superior because the Prophet rode—reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the practical application of the Prophet's Sunnah as a benchmark for excellence in worship. It distinguishes between the permissibility of walking and the higher merit of riding, aligning with the broader Islamic principle of following the Prophet's habitual practices in ritual acts.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Fazalat Bin Ayoub, from Rafa’at who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the walking of Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> (was it) from Makkah or from Al-Medina. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘From Makkah’.
And I asked him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘When I visit the House (Kabah), should I ride or walk?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Al-Hassan<sup>asws</sup> used to visit riding’. 
And I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the riding, whether it is superior, or the walking?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The riding’. I said, ‘The riding is superior than walking?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes, because Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> rode’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from Fadalah ibn Ayyub from Rifa‘ah who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and his walking on foot; if it was from Makkah or al-Madinah. He (the Imam) said, ‘It was from Makkah.’ I then asked, ‘If I visit the House, should I walk on foot or riding?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would visit riding.’ I then asked, ‘Is riding more virtuous or walking on foot?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Riding is more virtuous than walking on foot because the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, did so riding.’”
